reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that receiver efficiency is governed by two interrelated factors: route separation and coverage constraint. Route separation, defined as the average deviation of individual routes from the mean, directly correlates with YAC/E and air-yd share. This is captured by ΔS = Σ(sᵢ − s_avg)/n. Coverage constraint, C, measures how much defensive positioning limits receiver space, modeled as a sum of normalized deficits in active coverage. When C < 0.4, separation advantage becomes critical. The tendency break signal, T, captures behavioral shifts in targeting when matchups deviate significantly from expected norms. These three primitives form a triadic system where ΔS and C define the geometric and tactical landscape, while T encodes the cognitive response to it. Failure modes include when C approaches zero (over-constrained) or when T drops below threshold (predictable play-calling). Dualities emerge between separation and coverage depth, and between behavioral signals and strategic intent. The system exhibits nonlinearity in high-separation regimes where coverage cannot scale proportionally.
